- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day horizons.
- When sentiment is negative (even mildly, e.g., -0.25), model should adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% across all forecasted days to reflect market pessimism.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — apply a “lagged mean reversion” rule: if forecast > true outcome by >3%, reduce subsequent forecasts by 0.3–0.7% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sharp downward trends early — add a “mean reversion buffer” to the first 5–7 days of forecast, especially if recent history shows volatility.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive and model forecasts are rising, check for “overconfidence bias” — cap upward forecasts at 1.5–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid runaway spikes.
